title: Three Ranges
statement: The integers $x$, $y$ and $z$ satisfy $-6 \le x \le 2$, $-5 \le y \le 3$ and $1 \le z \le 4$. What is the smallest possible value of the product $x \cdot y \cdot z$?
hints: Since $z$ is always positive, look at the sign of $x \cdot y$. Which signs must $x$ and $y$ have for the whole product to be negative? Notice that taking the largest sizes, $x = -6$ and $y = -5$, gives a positive product.
Use casework on the signs. For a negative product, $x$ and $y$ must have opposite signs, so either $x < 0 < y$ or $y < 0 < x$. In each case, find the largest possible size of $x \cdot y$.

If $x < 0 < y$, the most negative value of $x \cdot y$ is $(-6) \cdot 3 = -18$. If $y < 0 < x$, it is $2 \cdot (-5) = -10$. Since $z$ is positive, a larger $z$ makes a negative product more negative, so now choose $z$.
solution: Since $z>0$, a negative product needs $xy<0$. If $x<0<y$ then $|xy|\le 6\cdot 3=18$. If $y<0<x$ then $|xy|\le 2\cdot 5=10$. So $xyz\ge -18\cdot 4=-72$ whenever the product is negative, and this bound holds trivially otherwise. Equality holds at $x=-6$, $y=3$, $z=4$, so the minimum is $-72$.
